note: Guides are written in the authors' own words from the official trophy descriptions and general GTA knowledge. The game had not released when this guide was written, so each guide only promises what its official description promises and flags where a detail is still unconfirmed.

trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.guide: This is the platinum trophy, and it unlocks automatically once you have earned the other 54 trophies on the list. There is nothing extra to do for it beyond finishing everything else, so treat it as the finish line of the whole guide. Follow the roadmap in order — story first, then stranger strands, activities, collectibles, and finally the cleanup trophies — and this one pops last.

trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.guide: Play through the opening mission, Gone Fishing, from start to finish. It is the first story mission of the game, so you cannot miss it: just follow the on-screen objectives until the mission completes. The trophy pops as soon as the mission's end screen appears.

trophies.name: Paradise Lost
trophies.guide: Play every story mission in Chapter 1 until the chapter closes. Chapters in GTA games end after a set run of missions, so keep taking the next story mission marker on the map until the chapter-complete moment. If you get stuck on a mission, retry it from the pause menu — progress in the chapter is kept.

trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
trophies.guide: Finish all of Chapter 2's story missions in order. New missions appear on the map as the previous one ends, so keep following the story markers rather than wandering off into side content. The trophy unlocks when the chapter's final mission ends and the story moves on to Chapter 3.

trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
trophies.guide: Complete the story missions of Chapter 3. By this point the map has opened up considerably, so it is easy to get distracted — but the chapter only ends when its missions are done, so prioritise the story markers. The trophy pops at the end of the chapter's last mission.

trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
trophies.guide: Play through Chapter 4's missions to their conclusion. This is the last numbered chapter, so expect its missions to be longer and tougher than the earlier ones; stock up on armour and ammo before the big set pieces. The trophy unlocks when the chapter ends and the story heads into its finale.

trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
trophies.guide: Finish the game's final story mission. It only becomes available after Chapter 4 is complete, so this is one of the last story trophies you will earn. Go in prepared — final missions in GTA games are usually long, multi-stage affairs — and the gold trophy pops when the credits roll. After it, the open world stays available for cleanup.

trophies.name: Trust
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission called Breakfast Run. It appears as a story marker on the map when the plot reaches it, so just play the story in order until it shows up. Follow the mission's objectives to the end and the trophy unlocks on completion.

trophies.name: Break the Bank
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission The Cartel Heist. Heist missions in GTA games usually need some setup first, so expect a few lead-up steps before the heist itself. Finish the heist and escape as the mission directs, and the trophy pops when it ends.

trophies.name: Family Matters
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Child's Play when it appears in the story. Play the missions in order and the marker will show up on its own — there is no special trigger to hunt for. The trophy unlocks the moment the mission completes.

trophies.name: DWNFALL
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Headliners. Like the other named-mission trophies, this one is unmissable as long as you play the story through — the mission marker appears when the plot reaches it. Follow the objectives to the end and the trophy pops.

trophies.name: Hi-Jacked
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission VCIA Takedown, set around Vice City International Airport. Expect a combat-heavy mission given the name, so go in with a full weapon loadout and armour. The trophy unlocks when the mission's final objective is done.

trophies.name: Snow Storm
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Operation Savage Glory. The name suggests a large-scale operation, so expect several stages and heavy resistance. Play it through to the end — checkpoints keep your progress if you fail a stage — and the trophy pops on completion.

trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.guide: Reach 100% completion, which in GTA games means finishing the story plus a defined checklist of side content — stranger missions, activities, collectibles and hidden packages, as tracked on the in-game stats screen. This is a late-game gold: work through the roadmap's phases and check the stats screen regularly to see what is still missing. It is the hardest trophy on the list after the platinum itself, so leave it for the cleanup phase.

trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.guide: Pull off 250 stunts in total — jumps, near misses, long airtime and the like, as the game counts them. Stunts accumulate across the whole playthrough, so a lot of this total will build up naturally while you drive between missions. To finish it off, pick a fast car or bike, find a jump or ramp, and repeat runs: the counter is cumulative, so every stunt counts toward the 250.

trophies.name: Master of None
trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Try every type of side activity the game offers at least once — races, shooting range, fishing, arcade games, drone races and whatever else appears on the map or in the activities menu. You only need one attempt at each type, not a win, so just sample them all. Check the in-game stats or activity list to see which types you have not tried yet, and tick them off one by one.

trophies.name: The Shootist
trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Visit a shooting range and earn a gold medal in every one of its challenges. Each challenge scores you on accuracy and speed, so take it slow at first to learn the targets, then push for speed once you know the layout. Gold thresholds are usually tight, so retry a challenge as many times as you need — attempts are unlimited and the range is always open.

trophies.name: Top Fun
trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Win a Top Fun drone race at each of its locations across Leonida. Drone races are found at marked spots on the map; fly the course through the checkpoints and finish ahead of the rival drones. Learn each course with a practice run first, then race for the win — you need a victory at every location, not just one.

trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
trophies.guide: Win 20 different races — each race you win must be a different event, not the same one repeated. Races are scattered across Leonida on land, and probably on water and in the air too; check the map for race markers. Pick a vehicle suited to each race, learn the route on a first attempt, then go for the win. Keep a mental list of the ones you have already won so you do not waste time re-running them.

trophies.name: Baited My Tackle
trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Take on Cal in a fishing challenge and beat him. Fishing challenges are found at fishing spots around Leonida; Cal is a named rival you meet there. Pay attention to the fishing mechanics — line tension, reeling rhythm and bait choice all matter — and keep at it until you out-fish him. The trophy pops when you win the challenge against him.

trophies.name: Stick Fiddler
trophies.guide: Find an arcade — there are arcade machines in bars and arcades around Vice City — and play one game through to its end. You do not need a high score or a win, just a full playthrough of a single arcade game. Pick the simplest game on offer if you just want the trophy quickly, and the trophy pops when the game ends.

trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Finish the last mission in Andy's strand of stranger missions. Andy's missions appear as a stranger marker on the map once you meet him; work through his strand in order, mission by mission. The trophy unlocks when his final mission ends. Stranger strands are easy to leave half-done, so keep an eye on the map for his marker between story missions.

trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide: Complete Kenton's stranger-mission strand, ending with his final mission. The name hints at a boat, so expect at least part of his strand to take place on the water around Leonida. Follow his marker on the map through each mission in turn, and the trophy pops when the last one is done.

trophies.name: The Lone Rider
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide: Finish Billy's strand of stranger missions with his final mission. The title suggests a biker, so his missions likely involve bikes and the open road — bring a fast bike when his marker calls. Work through his strand in order and the trophy unlocks at the end of the last mission.

trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks
trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: Complete eight full stranger-mission strands across Leonida. Strangers appear as question-mark markers on the map; each one opens a short chain of missions, and a strand only counts once its final mission is done. There are more than eight strangers in the state, so pick the strands you enjoy and finish them completely. This is a silver for a reason — it takes real time — so work on it steadily alongside the story rather than leaving all eight for the end.

trophies.name: Supply & Demand
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Complete Randy's stranger-mission strand, finishing with his final mission. The name suggests supply runs and deliveries, so expect driving work with cargo to protect or deliver. Follow his map marker through the strand in order, and the trophy pops when the final mission ends.

trophies.name: Spin On This!
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide: Finish Tyrone's strand of stranger missions with his final mission. As with the other named strangers, his marker appears on the map once you meet him; play his missions in order until the strand closes. The trophy unlocks at the end of his final mission.

trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude
trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: Find every meditation spot across Leonida and meditate at each one. Meditation spots are quiet scenic locations — hilltops, beaches, viewpoints — usually marked on the map or discoverable while exploring. Visit each spot and use the meditate prompt there; the trophy pops once you have done them all. This pairs well with the exploration trophy, so do both on the same map sweep.

trophies.name: Fair Game
trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Take on a hunting task for Bret and bring down the unique animal he wants. Hunting in GTA games means tracking the animal in the wild — watch for tracks, sounds and the hunting prompt — then making a clean kill. The animal is unique, so it only appears in its own area; follow Bret's directions to find it, and the trophy pops once the hunt is complete.

trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck
trophies.guide: Collect trading cards scattered around Leonida and complete three full sets. Cards are hidden in shops, interiors and out-of-the-way spots; a set is complete when you hold every card in it. You will find cards naturally while exploring, but finishing three sets means actively hunting the missing ones — keep a checklist of which cards each set still needs. The trophy pops the moment the third set is complete.

trophies.name: You WAiNKer!
trophies.guide: Use the WAiNK It feature — the game's photo or social-sharing mode — at 100 different locations. The counter counts distinct places, so revisit the same spot does not help: you need to WAiNK It in 100 separate locations across Leonida. Fold this into exploration — snap one at every new area, landmark and viewpoint you pass — and the total will climb steadily. The trophy pops at location number 100.

trophies.name: One Last Thing
trophies.guide: Complete 50 challenges in total. Challenges are the game's small optional objectives — stunt jumps, time trials, hidden tasks and the like — listed in the challenges menu. They accumulate across the whole playthrough, so many will complete themselves while you play; for the rest, open the challenges list, pick the easiest unfinished ones, and work through them. The trophy pops at challenge number 50.

trophies.name: Hot Together
trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: With your partner alongside you, build up a 4-star wanted level and then lose the police completely. Get the heat up by committing crimes with your partner in the car or on foot, then break line of sight and hide until the wanted stars flash and clear. Use the map's police view cone to plan an escape route, and fast vehicles or water help a lot. The trophy pops once the 4-star level is fully lost while your partner is with you.

trophies.name: Retail Therapy
trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: With your partner, rob three shops in a row without ever losing your wanted level between robberies. Plan a route past three shops close together, keep a fast getaway car parked outside each one, and move quickly — the trick is to keep the wanted level alive from the first robbery to the third. Do not let the stars clear, and do not get caught or killed. The trophy pops after the third shop.

trophies.name: Whip It Good
trophies.guide: Discover 100 different vehicles — drive or ride a vehicle for the first time and it counts as discovered. The total covers cars, bikes, boats and aircraft, so variety is the fastest route: try a new vehicle every time you see one instead of sticking to your favourite car. Car parks, docks, airfields and traffic all hold new finds, and the trophy pops at vehicle number 100.

trophies.name: Gunslinger
trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Activate Combat Focus — the game's slow-motion aiming mode — and take down five enemies before it ends. The easiest setup is a spot with a cluster of enemies, such as a gang hideout or a shootout in a mission, where five targets are close together. Wait until several enemies are in view, trigger Combat Focus, and work through them quickly with headshots. The trophy pops as soon as the fifth enemy drops inside the same use.

trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can
trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: Head to Vice City International Airport and leave in a way the airport did not schedule — in plain terms, steal a plane and take off without following the normal route. Get airside, take a plane from the runway or a hangar, and get airborne while the airport reacts. Any aircraft that gets you off the ground from VCIA should do it, and the trophy pops once you are away.

trophies.name: Challenging Tank
trophies.guide: Get involved with Rhino tanks — the description's joke is that it is hot inside one. In GTA games the Rhino is the military tank, usually found at the army base or called in at high wanted levels. Steal one, drive one, or survive an encounter with them: the trophy is tied to the Rhino itself, so head to wherever the military keeps its armour in Leonida. The exact trigger is not spelled out in the official description, so expect it to pop from simply getting into a Rhino or taking one on.

trophies.name: Sneakthief
trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Rob a jewelry store without ever being detected. Go in quietly — avoid the cameras and the staff's line of sight, move slowly, and take the goods without raising an alarm. If you are spotted, the attempt fails, so leave and try again rather than fighting your way out. A stealthy approach and patience are the whole trick, and the trophy pops once the robbery is done clean.

trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal
trophies.guide: Rob five bank vaults and escape after each one. Bank vault robberies are major jobs — crack the vault, grab the cash, and get clear of the police before the trophy counts that vault. Each vault only counts if you escape, so plan a getaway vehicle and route before you go in. Work through the banks one at a time; the silver pops after the fifth successful escape.

trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play
trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Find an armored truck on the roads of Leonida, rob it, and escape. Armored trucks drive set routes — look for them on highways and in the city — then stop the truck, break it open and take the cash. The police will respond fast, so have a getaway car ready and lose the wanted level to finish the job. The trophy pops once you have escaped clean.

trophies.name: The Goodtime State
trophies.guide: Explore every part of Leonida — the whole state, from Vice City to the swamps, beaches and countryside. The game tracks which areas you have visited, so you need to set foot in each named area at least once. Drive the highways, take the back roads, and check the map for blank patches you have never visited. Pair this with the meditation spots and the WAiNK It locations on one big map sweep, and the trophy pops when the last area is discovered.

trophies.name: Pest Control
trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Find and rob an illegal operation belonging to each gang in Leonida. Gangs run their own rackets — drug labs, chop shops, smuggling dens — and each gang's operation is in its own turf, so this trophy is really a tour of the state's criminal map. Hit one operation per gang and get away clean; the trophy pops once every gang has been hit at least once.

trophies.name: In The Beginning…
trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: Go to Ocean Beach in Vice City, find a beachfront bar, and order a cocktail to enjoy with the view. This is a pure flavour trophy — no skill or combat involved — and it is named for the series' famous first beach. Sit down, order the drink, and the trophy pops once the moment plays out.

trophies.name: Capital Offense
trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: Drive a car into — and then out through the glass of — a vehicle showroom, in the classic GTA style. Pick a showroom with a big glass front, get a fast car, and smash straight through the window to the street. The trophy is a nod to the series' famous showroom escapes, so the more dramatic the exit the better; it pops once you break out.

trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling
trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: Visit the Kolt & Associates bowling alley and play a game of bowling through to the end — the 'follow-through' in the description is the bowling motion. This is a callback to the series' famous bowling dates: just play a full game at that alley. You do not need a particular score, only a completed game, and the trophy pops when it ends.

trophies.name: Personal Best
trophies.guide: This trophy is tied to a partnership moment with your in-game partner that draws a crowd — the description is deliberately vague, so the exact trigger is not spelled out in the official text. The sensible reading is a story or partner activity where the pair's antics attract attention, so keep playing partner content and co-op moments as they come. If it has not popped by the end of the story, revisit partner activities and public stunts with your partner alongside you.

trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder
trophies.guide: Make story choices when the game offers them — the description says choices made, for better or worse, and the trophy tracks the decisions you take along the way. Choices in GTA games appear at key story moments, and some can only be made once per playthrough, so think before you pick: there is no confirmed way to redo a choice without replaying the mission or the story. This is one of the few trophies flagged missable here for exactly that reason — if a choice moment passes, it may not come back. Make your choices deliberately and the trophy pops once the tracked choices are done.

trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess
trophies.guide: Succeed at something on your second attempt — the description's joke is that the first try went wrong. In practice this means failing a task, then completing it on the immediate retry. The honest warning is that this is missable in spirit: if you succeed at everything first time, there is no second try to charm. If you fail a mission, challenge or event, do not reload an old save — just retry and finish it, and the trophy should pop on the successful second attempt.

trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There
trophies.guide: Witness something strange — the description suggests a one-off weird event, in the series' long tradition of UFOs, ghosts and odd encounters hidden around the map. These events are usually tied to a specific place and time, and they may not repeat if you walk away, so this trophy is flagged missable: if something strange happens in front of you, stay and watch it play out. Explore odd landmarks, visit them at night, and keep an eye out for anything that does not belong.

trophies.name: Ten Pin
trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: Knock someone over with a melee attack from a moving vehicle — a melee drive-by. Get a passenger or a slow-moving vehicle, pull up beside a pedestrian, and swing a melee weapon from the car as you pass. It takes a bit of timing: drive slowly enough to connect, fast enough to count as a drive-by. Any pedestrian target works, and the trophy pops when one goes down to the hit.

trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar
trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Launder $250,000 worth of Marked Bills through your contacts. Marked Bills are dirty money you pick up from robberies and heists; your contacts clean them for a cut. Keep feeding bills through your laundering contacts over the course of the game — the total is cumulative, so it builds up with every robbery and heist. The trophy pops once $250,000 has been cleaned in total.

trophies.name: Treat Yo Self
trophies.guide: Spend $100,000 in total across all shops — clothes, weapons, car mods, food, anything the shops sell. The total is cumulative across every shop, so normal spending across a playthrough gets you most of the way there. Late in the game, if you are short, buy big-ticket items like weapon upgrades or car customisation to close the gap. The trophy pops once your lifetime shop spending passes $100,000.

trophies.name: Little Boxes
trophies.guide: Buy every garage property available in Leonida. Garages are properties you purchase to store vehicles, and they are sold through the in-game property or real-estate listings. They cost serious money, so this is a late-game trophy: save up, check the property listings regularly, and buy each garage as it becomes available. The trophy pops when the last garage is yours.

trophies.name: On the Spot
trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app — the game's delivery or rideshare app, judging by the name. Take a vehicle, open the app, and register it; repeat with nine more different vehicles. Any vehicles you drive can likely be registered, so fold this into the vehicle-discovery trophy and register each new find as you go. The trophy pops at the tenth registration.
